adversarial_review.check: The hostile lane supplies alpha=1 to the mixed helper and it rejects the divergent-tail case.
A reversed toy spectrum changes both the quadratic and optimized mixed envelopes.
Multiplying by lambda^alpha instead of dividing by lambda^alpha changes the counting constant and fails.
Changing the interior split changes the finite mixed bound, so an off-by-one cannot be silent.
A linear k constant inserted into the retained quadratic envelope yields a negative toy residual.
The first positive inverse eigenvalue is strictly below the full inverse-spectrum trace on both selected rows.
Exactly d-1 positive modes above the declared floor are required; a diagonal generator gives no edges or positive spectrum.
The finite head and tail sums are checked before the UV integral remainder; the infinite value is not a finite equality.
The non-importing lane agrees on invariant aggregate fields within 5e-6; optimizer histograms are not promoted because tied minimizers can swap under roundoff.
A row-wise best pair and split do not imply a fixed rule or uniform constants, a common core, GNS coercivity, a physical gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite mixed IR/UV spectral-counting and zeta-tail checkpoint only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform bound, common core, common split rule, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
decision_reason: Splitting the ordered spectrum into an infrared head and ultraviolet tail allows separate sublinear exponents and makes the finite trace budget explicit without assuming a common alpha. Primary, independent, hostile, integrated and Lean checks validate the finite implication, while no data establish a regulator-independent split or constants.
finding: The primary lane passes 592762/592762 assertions over 7 systems, 2688 contexts and 21120 conditional rows; the independent lane passes 592762/592762; the hostile lane passes 9/9; the integrated verifier passes 55/55; and Lean R412 compiles. Every row enumerates all 25 declared exponent pairs and every interior split. The selected finite mixed envelope ranges over [0.5800949275086398,2.117318722273093] and the selected infinite comparison over [0.6295715327320223,3.1299469867610137].
method: For every actual conditional likelihood row, form W=D_pi^(-1/2)L D_pi^(-1/2) and sort its d-1 positive eigenvalues.
For each declared exponent pair and every interior split, compute separate IR and UV counting constants and the finite head/tail envelope.
Compare only the UV tail with its explicit integral remainder for reciprocal exponent greater than one.
Repeat the full volume-two cutoff, beta, source, history, order, prefix, adjoint and collar-orientation grid in independent code.
Use alpha=1, unsorted, split-index, exponent-inverted, linear-scaling, Fiedler-only and diagonal-generator mutations as hostile controls, then run the Lean scalar cross-check.
next_action: Prove a fixed or analytically controlled IR/UV split rule and positive uniform bounds for both counting constants on one Hamiltonian common core; control cutoff, volume, source, phase and exhaustion dependence; transfer to the R-399 shell and combine with the R-406 Schur residual split.
no_overclaim: The mixed exponent family is a finite spectral inequality and a broader uniformity target; it is not an analytic regulator estimate, thermodynamic theorem, physical-sector result or QFT mass-gap proof.

qft_interface.closed: Finite spectral ordering, all declared mixed exponent/split envelopes, UV zeta-tail comparison, full likelihood-row coverage, hostile shortcut rejection and Lean scalar bookkeeping.
qft_interface.open: Uniform split rule and constants on a common Hamiltonian core, phase selection, shell transfer, common-alpha dynamics, broken-sector GNS coercivity, continuum and physical-gap obligations.

question: Can an IR/UV mixed spectral-counting envelope control the normalized Green trace without imposing one common finite exponent, and can its split rule be made uniform on the physical route?
title: Two-regime IR/UV mixed spectral-counting envelope for the normalized Green trace
